hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation of the product as built
hard_gates.evidence:
No leak found. As alnoor's admin I attacked gulfsteel with 96 calls (attacks/g1-attack.mjs, g1-a-vs-b.txt). The targets were B's admin and 3 users (GET record, access, sign-ins, default-company, passkeys; PUT; password; unblock; sessions/revoke; default-company PUT; DELETE passkeys; DELETE), 3 of B's roles (GET, PUT, copy, DELETE), B's new passkey through /me/passkeys/{id} (GET, PUT, DELETE), and B's saved and shared list views (GET, PUT, DELETE). Every call answered 404 or 400. Tenant-switch headers and query fields (x-tenant-id, x-tenant, x-workspace, ?tenant=, ?workspace=) were ignored. A hash of B's users, roles, user_roles and passkeys was the same before and after.

Passkey sign-in: I used a software ES256 authenticator I wrote (attacks/softpasskey.mjs). A's key under handles naming B's admin, A's key with B's credential id, and A's key with a handle naming no workspace all gave byte-identical 401 auth.passkeyFailed answers. B's own passkey signs in (200), and replaying the same answer is refused (401).

Differential checks: B's ids against random ids in view PUT, roleIds, companyRoles[].companyId, the role filter and the usersByRole report parameter. Every pair answered the same (g1-differential.txt).

Exports: users, roles, usersByRole and roleSummary as CSV, XLSX (unzipped) and PDF, in English and Arabic, held no gulfsteel data.

Database (db-app-role.txt), as erp_app:
- With no tenant bound, and with a session-wide set_config, it sees 0 rows.
- Bound to A, it sees 100,005 users and 1 passkey, 0 of them from other tenants.
- UPDATE of B's users and passkeys changed 0 rows. An INSERT into B's passkeys was refused by RLS.
- DISABLE RLS, SET ROLE erp_owner and row_security=off were all refused. No erp role has bypassrls.
- identity.passkeys has RLS enabled and forced, with only the standard tenant_isolation policy.

hard_gates.gate: G1 gate catches tenant leaks planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence:
Plants are in plants/apply-r8-plants.py and plants/r8-plants-run1.diff. They ran through verify-slot (plants/run1/gates.log).
- L7, a database leak: an extra PERMISSIVE SELECT policy on identity.passkeys that opens every workspace's passkeys when no tenant is bound ('so passkey sign-in finds the credential first'). Caught by G1DatabaseIsolationTests ('identity.passkeys: 2 rows visible without a tenant' and 'unreviewed policy passkeys_before_workspace'), G1TenantSettingCodeTests and G1TenantSourceTests.
- L8, a process-state leak: the PasskeyChallenges singleton remembers offered credentials per e-mail address and adds them to excludeCredentials, so a same-address user in tenant A is handed tenant B's credential ids. Caught by G1ProcessStateTests ('singleton ...PasskeyChallenges._offered: a read-only field that holds a mutable ConcurrentDictionary') and by G1HttpIsolationTests ('Process-wide state changed while the tenants used the app ... _offered[admin@bravo-...]').

biggest_gap.title: A lost or stolen device keeps signing in: 'Reset password' and 'Sign out everywhere' leave the user's passkeys working, and no administrator screen shows or removes them
biggest_gap.detail:
This round added passkeys: a user adds one in My account and then signs in with one device confirmation. The administrator's levers on the users screen did not grow with it.

When an employee's laptop is lost or stolen, an administrator does what the user panel offers: 'Reset password…' ("Password reset. N sessions ended.") and 'Sign out everywhere'. The passkey on the lost laptop still signs in straight afterwards (200).

The user panel's tabs (Details, What they can do, Sign-in history) never mention passkeys. The sign-in history does not say whether a sign-in used a passkey or a password. The API has GET and DELETE /api/identity/users/{id}/passkeys, summarised as being 'for a lost device, a person leaving', but no screen calls them. The only screen lever that works is deactivating the account, which also locks out the person.

For a UAE trading company with shared or field laptops, this makes the scope's 'reset password, lockout' unsafe for exactly the case it exists for.

Fix:
- Show a user's passkeys (name, created, last used) in the user panel, with 'Remove all passkeys' for users within the caller's access. That is the existing DELETE, Arabic included.
- Have 'Reset password' (or a tick box on it) and 'Sign out everywhere' offer to remove passkeys too, and say so in the done message.
- Record the sign-in method in the sign-in history.
- Add an e2e test: after reset plus sign-out-everywhere plus remove, the device's passkey answers 401.
biggest_gap.evidence:
In the seeded demo (./erp up), run node gauntlet/evidence/p03-identity/r8/attacks/lost-device.mjs (uses softpasskey.mjs) against the demo URL. Output (attacks/lost-device.txt):

- Only deactivation stops it: 'passkey sign-in after deactivation: 401'

Screen: walks/walk7.mjs opens the viewer, who holds the passkey 'Critic virtual key' added in walk6 through a Chromium virtual authenticator. It reports "tabs mentioning a passkey: []" (screenshot 12). web/src/modules/identity/UserPanel.tsx has 0 occurrences of 'passkey', and the only callers of /passkeys are in PasskeysSection.tsx (the user's own).

[route: p00-foundation] The ratchet's verify.quietSeconds judges a run 'quiet' from two load samples, at start and end.
